title: Universal flatness open for a morphism between relative families
statement: Let $S,X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $p:X\to S$, $q:Y\to S$ and $f:X\to Y$ be morphisms with $q\circ f=p$. Assume $p$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and a closed map on underlying topological spaces, meaning that it sends every closed subset to a closed subset. Assume $q$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $U=\{x\in |X|:f\text{ is flat at }x\}$ and $F=|S|\setminus p(|X|\setminus U)$. Then $F$ is open and, equipped with the restricted structure sheaf, defines an open subscheme $F\hookrightarrow S$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. For every scheme $T$ and morphism $h:T\to S$, the base change $f_T:X\times_ST\to Y\times_ST$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is flat if and only if $h$ factors through $F\hookrightarrow S$.

source.place: Tag 05XB, spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-where-flat, statement and displayed construction of W in its proof, specialized to schemes; relative source locus input is Tag 05VK (more-morphisms-lemma-base-change-flatness-fibres).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-flat-locus-base-change] to $p,q,f$. Its hypotheses are precisely that $p$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, $q$ is locally of finite type, and $qf=p$, all assumed here. Thus $U$ is open and for every $h:T\to S$ the flat locus of $f_T$ is $\pi_X^{-1}(U)$, where $\pi_X:X_T\to X$ is the projection.

source.place: Tag 05XB, lemma-where-flat, first sentence of proof; scheme input Tag 05VK, more-morphisms-lemma-base-change-flatness-fibres.

proof.text: Put $C=|X|\setminus U$. Since $C$ is closed and $p$ is a closed map, $p(C)$ is closed, so $F=|S|\setminus p(C)$ is open. Give $F$ the restricted structure sheaf. To check that this is a scheme, take an affine chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ around any $s\in F$. The principal-open basis gives $s\in D(a)\subset V\cap F$; the principal-localization open immersion identifies this ringed open with $\operatorname{Spec}A_a$. These affine neighbourhoods cover $F$, so the scheme definition applies. The inclusion with this restricted sheaf is an open immersion by its definition.

source.place: Tag 05XB, lemma-where-flat, displayed construction of W and openness argument; Schemes Tag 01IK, lemma-open-subspace-scheme, elementary affine-neighbourhood proof.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary scheme $T$ and $h:T\to S$, and write $p_T:X_T\to T$ for the projection. Step 1 shows that the nonflat locus of $f_T$ is $\pi_X^{-1}(C)$, by taking complements. The subset image identity for the cartesian square defining $X_T$ gives $p_T(\pi_X^{-1}(C))=h^{-1}(p(C))$. By the definition of flat morphism, $f_T$ is flat exactly when its nonflat locus is empty. A subset is empty exactly when its image under a function is empty. Therefore $f_T$ is flat if and only if $h^{-1}(p(C))=\varnothing$, equivalently $h(|T|)\subseteq F$. This uses neither closedness of $p_T$ nor any finiteness assumption on $T$.

source.place: Tag 05XB, lemma-where-flat, final sentence expanded using Morphisms Tag 01S1, lemma-base-change-surjective, subset image identity in its proof.

proof.text: If $h(|T|)\subseteq F$, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] applied to the open subscheme of step 2 gives a morphism $T\to F$ whose composite with $F\hookrightarrow S$ is $h$. Conversely such a factorization has image contained in $F$, since the inclusion has image $F$. Combining this with step 3 proves the required equivalence for every $T$ and $h$.

source.place: Tag 05XB, lemma-where-flat, final sentence; Schemes Tag 01HI, lemma-restrict-map-to-opens.
